To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

the power dissipation of an analog circuit is directly related to the product of the input signal amplitude and the bandwidth of the circuit; and that the input signal amplitude can be reduced by a factor of 10 or more by using a low impedance input circuit and a high impedance signal processing section.
a low impedance level is not required for fast pulse circuits and that a low impedance circuit can be designed for low power operation if the circuit is properly designed.

(1) a high impedance, low power, fast pulse amplifier circuit can be designed and built; (2) the circuit can operate at high speed (3 ns) and low power (350 mw) with an input impedance of 1000 ohms; (3) the circuit can be used in a large number of different applications.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the design of circuits that will operate at low power levels and yet respond to input pulses in the 1 to 10 ns time range.
the application of low power techniques to the handling of fast pulses in a gamma-ray telescope.
the development of techniques for handling short pulses at low power levels.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the low power fast pulse circuit techniques described in this paper are applicable to a wide range of problems in electronics.
the design techniques used in the Gamma-Ray Telescope electronics are not new but rather a combination of many techniques used in other areas of electronics.
the design of the analog portion of this system is based upon a thorough knowledge of the circuitry involved, and upon an understanding of the requirements imposed on the system.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

the circuitry of the MIT Gamma-ray Telescope, which has been in operation on board the OSO-3 satellite since 1965, has demonstrated that low impedance circuits, which are normally associated with high power consumption, can be designed to operate at low power levels.
we have been able to achieve a power consumption of only one-tenth of that which would have resulted if we had followed a conventional design approach.
the design of the Gamma-Ray electronics has demonstrated that it is possible to achieve a low-power fast pulse circuit with the required performance.
The main takeaway from our work is that
it is possible to design a low power fast pulse circuit with a high degree of success.
it is possible to design fast pulse handling circuits with very low power consumption.
the use of low power circuits is possible in fast pulse handling applications.
